subject: Licensing alignment + vendor technical eval for Sales engagement tools
messages: Subject: Re-evaluating our Sales engagement stack ahead of Q3 renewals

Hi team,

We have a couple of renewals across our engagement stack coming up (Outreach contract up 8/15, and a smaller Salesloft pilot that ends 9/1). Finance just flagged that our baseline seat count has drifted and Legal wants an updated T&Cs intake before renewals.

I want to propose a short internal + vendor technical evaluation so we can make a consolidation decision (if any) by mid-July. Objectives:
- Confirm current seat usage and projected needs for 2028
- Run an integration compatibility check with SFDC & Redwood event pipeline
- Capture pricing/discount path and any data residency / compliance caveats

Lauren — can you pull the seat ledger and current PO terms? Jonas — can you scope a 2-3 day integration health check (hooks, webhooks, API rate limits, token rotation)? Marissa — please pre-flag any CS or renewal conversations you already have in flight with Outreach or Salesloft contacts.

Ideally we coordinate vendor evals the week of 6/21 so we have time to negotiate before Finance deadlines. I attached an initial checklist (engagement-integration-checklist.xlsx) for the integration scope.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachment: engagement-integration-checklist.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 140KB)
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating our Sales engagement stack ahead of Q3 renewals

Thanks Ben — pulling numbers now. Quick notes from my side:
- Outreach renewal: current term runs 8/15/2027; we bill annually. Baseline seats 120 (we have 15 overage seats flagged in last invoice).
- Salesloft pilot: 25 seats; pilot paid through 9/01/2027.
- Current Outreach SOW specifically calls out prefix-based activity caching and a custom webhook flow used by SDRs for cadence updates — that could be a sticky technical dependency.

I uploaded the current Outreach PO & last invoice to the Drive folder (link below). I've also flagged Legal to pre-read the redline items; they asked for any vendor security docs (SOC2) up front.

Will share the seat ledger by EOD today. Jonas — I added a tab in the checklist for token/auth patterns — please add your rate-limit tests.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Procurement Manager, Revenue Tools
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Outreach-PO-2026.pdf (PDF, 85KB)
Cc: Outreach Sales Ops <salesops@outreach.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Subject: Outreach renewal & consolidation options — preliminary quote

Hi Ben — great to connect last week on the renewal timing. I pulled together a short note with options based on the numbers you mentioned:

Option A (Renew):
- Maintain current footprint (120 baseline + 15 overage seats)
- List price: $xxx,xxx/year; outreach standard renewal discounts for 12-month term (10%); includes API support SLA at enterprise tier

Option B (Consolidate + Term):
- Consolidate Salesloft pilot into Outreach (convert 25 seats) and commit to a 24-month term for blended pricing
- Blended list: $xxx,xxx/year with a 20% commitment discount and a one-time integration credit

Security & compliance: we can provide SOC2 Type II report and our data handling annex. We also support customer-managed key patterns though that requires an elevated contract addendum.

Attached is the preliminary quote (Outreach-quote-June2027.pdf) and a short appendix on API limits. If you want, we can set a 45-min technical call with our integrations engineer (I can include them on the thread).

Cheers,
Sarah Kim
Strategic AM, Outreach.io

Attachment: Outreach-quote-June2027.pdf (PDF, 126KB)

Subject: Re: Outreach renewal & consolidation options — preliminary quote

Thanks Sarah — this is exactly the kind of framing we needed. Next steps on our side:
1) Jonas to run the 2-day integration health check the week of 6/21 and report back on any API gaps (rate limits, webhook payload size, auth rotation).
2) Lauren will finalize seat ledger and proposed headcount forecast by 6/16 to anchor seat counts for negotiation.
3) Legal (cc'd) requested the SOC2 and the customer-managed key docs; Sarah, please share those two artifacts directly when possible.
4) We'll hold a 45-min technical session with your integrations engineer the week of 6/21 — can you propose 2 time slots?

High-level negotiation strategy (internal):
- Push for a blended 24-month commitment only if integration findings are clean and Finance signs off on the cost model.
- Ask for a one-time migration/integration credit to cover our internal engineering hours (target: 40-80h).
- Reserve the right to stagger seat buy-in to reduce upfront cash burn in Q3.

Marissa — please surface any active renewal conversations or concessions Outreach already offered. Legal — if you can standby to review the SOC2 and the KMS addendum when Sarah sends them, that would speed the loop.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference
